text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Flood forces out 6,200 more: Winnipeg suburbs under threat.
- Liberals offer to spend more on health care: Opponents warn against gullibility as Chretien does about-face on cuts.
- Officer guilty in Ipperwash killing: Judge rejects testimony about events leading up to shooting of native protester.
- Rwandan refugees emerge from hiding: Hunger force thousands from jungle.
- Poor already behind by time they reach school: Early intervention programs operate on a shoestring, despite vast evidence about how human brain is shaped in first years.
- Cambridge to buy mall giant: Firm to make $375-million bid for Markborough in 'major thrust' to expand presence.
- Bay snags Wal-Mart veteran: Chain hires U.S. heavy hitter as CEO in face of heightened competition.
- Alberta regains optimism as good times return: With the economy surging and unemployment at a 15-year low, the talk on the street is of boom times again.
- Indonesia vows clampdown on junior explorers: No more Bre-X type ordeals: minister.
- Imasco sells Hardee's chain: Gets US$327-million for money-losing restaurants.
- $1.4 billion Cambridge swoop: Back on the growth trail, the Toronto real estate firm agrees to friendly takeover of Markborough Properties and takes on about $1 billion in debt.
- TD to launch cut-rate invasion of Europe.
